## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 43 (also known as the *Sabhojanasikkhāpada*) is an expiation rule within the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Theravāda tradition [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that a monk who intrudes and sits down uninvited in a household during meals or intimate relations (*yo pana bhikkhu sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjam kappeyya, pācittiyan ti*; Vin IV 95) commits a *pācittiya* offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Within the Theravāda collection, parallel formulations are found in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pc 43), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (Pc 43), and the corresponding lineage of nuns' rules (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pc 124, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pc 124, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pc 124) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies comprehensive parallels across other early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravādin rules preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive internal reuse with 79 other Pali Vinaya rules, showing the largest textual overlap with closely related rules such as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 46, 44, 45, 30, and Nissaggiya Pācittiya 18 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments in DharmaNexus correlate with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), the *Prātimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2), and Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* fragments, in agreement with the curated parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
